mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 4% for 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day rolling average of 60-day forward returns remains below the 10th percentile of similar labor strength regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth that outpaces supply, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in inventory levels (implied via supply chain stress) predicts a supply-side shock that depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative during confirmed supply disruptions.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5%, it indicates a shift toward restrictive policy, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in all post-crossing windows.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding increase in layoffs suggests a tight labor market that boosts investor sentiment and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months with no significant decline in employment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative during periods of sustained job openings without layoffs.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales (implied by consumer confidence proxies not present, so cannot use available proxies) — but since we must use available proxies, instead: A rapid increase in housing starts (not available, so fallback to demand via GDP components not available — thus we'll use a demand proxy) — instead using HOUST (utilization rate) rising by >2% in a month predicts demand expansion that supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls by more than 3% in a month while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 5%, it signals a supply-side contraction without labor market slack, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 3% in a month and UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive during such supply shocks.
